method: For the locally authored rooted AC1012 destination resave, compare physical R2000 ASCII CLASSES records from the intentionally unsafe guard-bypass/projection scratch build with ODA File Converter 27.1.0 output. Then convert the scratch DXF with ODA and inspect physical layout backlinks and CLASS rows.
observations: The diagnostic DXF emits DICTIONARYWDFLT and ACDBPLACEHOLDER classes, but no LAYOUT, GEODATA, RASTERVARIABLES or WIPEOUTVARIABLES class. The independent source object-map census reports two LAYOUT frames and no frames for the three proxy families in this source.

ODA's direct source conversion emits all four class names among other classes. Converting the diagnostic DXF through ODA retains both selected physical layout/backlink pairs and emits LAYOUT along with other classes, but does not add the three unused proxy-family classes.

Autodesk documents CLASSES for application-defined instances and the group-code meanings; this comparison does not establish whether an absent LAYOUT row is valid for the selected target or whether unused source CLASS rows may always be omitted.
limits: Scratch output bypassed three production guards and the legacy layout refusal; it is not a qualified export.
ODA conversion may add or repair records. No native AutoCAD, proxy ordinal, general class-table or binary-target conclusion follows.
